title: Restore safe rollout path after partial pin state left traffic stranded
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for a model rollout where a partial 'version pin' and a simultaneous routing-split left a subset of tenants receiving traffic routed to a pinned variant that had an incompatible runtime change. Rollback automation partially failed due to a concurrency and idempotency bug in the pin/unpin controller, causing elevated errors and tail latency for ~12 tenant routes for ~45 minutes. This ticket tracks investigation notes, temporary mitigations, and a prioritized list of action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-04 at 18:12 UTC, during a gradual model rollout that included a targeted version pin for a regulatory tenant cohort, routing-split and pin state updates were applied in overlapping operations. A race in the pin controller caused the pin to be applied on some replicas but not others, and the rollback automation attempted to revert the change but failed to clear the per-route pin state consistently. Impacted tenants experienced 5xx spikes and increased token latency when traffic hit the pinned variant that lacked a critical KV-cache upgrade. Manual mitigation required draining the pinned variant and re-routing traffic to a safe fallback. No data loss or PII exposure was detected.
timeline: 2026-03-04 18:05 UTC - Canary rollout initiated for model/v2026-03-04-a to 5% of traffic across regions
2026-03-04 18:12 UTC - Targeted pin operation started for tenant cohort TG-REG-21 (regulatory test group)
2026-03-04 18:13 UTC - Routing-split update (A/B split) applied concurrently by automated rollout engine
2026-03-04 18:18 UTC - Monitoring alerts: elevated 500s and p95/p99 latency for routes serving TG-REG-21
2026-03-04 18:19 UTC - Automatic rollback triggered by policy (error-rate threshold) but failed to fully clear per-route pin state
2026-03-04 18:21 UTC - On-call begins manual investigation; discovers inconsistent pin state across control plane replicas
2026-03-04 18:23 UTC - Manual mitigation: temporarily redirect TG-REG-21 to global fallback model (vstable) and drain pinned variant
2026-03-04 19:00 UTC - Error rates return to baseline after manual reroute; incident declared resolved at 19:02 UTC
2026-03-05 - Post-incident: replication of the bug in staging; root cause analysis begins
detection: Alerting via per-route SLO monitors (error-rate organ) and customer support tickets from TG-REG-21. SLO triggers combined with high tail latency in the rollout dashboard drew immediate attention. Pager duty alert to on-call platform engineer at 18:18 UTC.
impact: ~12 tenant routes affected; median request latency increased from 45ms to 380ms for affected routes, with 5xx rate peaking at 7% for ~45 minutes. A small number of requests resulted in client-visible errors requiring retries. No long-term data corruption or security breach.
root_cause: A race condition in the version-pin controller combined with non-idempotent rollback operations. The pin controller writes a per-route pin record and signals routing; when routing-split updates were applied concurrently, some control-plane replicas persisted the pin while others lost the transactional context. The rollback controller assumed a single-call unpin would be sufficient and did not reconcile partial states across replicas. Additionally, health gating for KV-cache compatibility (a preflight check) was not executed for pinned operations only applied to canary nodes.
mitigations: Immediate: manual drain of pinned variant and emergency reroute to stable model for affected tenants (completed)
Temporary: disable automated pin operations for targeted cohorts until controller fix is deployed (completed)
Monitoring: added an immediate synthetic check that validates per-route pin symmetry across all control plane replicas (deployed)
Communication: emailed impacted customers and logged incident in status page with RCA link (done)
action_items: Marco Nguyen | 2026-03-12 | Make pin/unpin controller idempotent: add reconciliation loop that re-checks pin state across replicas and retries with exponential backoff
Aisha Patel | 2026-03-19 | Add preflight compatibility check to rollout pipeline that validates KV-cache and runtime invariants on any variant that can be pinned
Lena Ortiz | 2026-03-21 | Extend integration tests to include concurrent pin + routing-split operations in the staging release harness
Sven Müller | 2026-03-18 | Harden rollback automation: ensure unpin operations are observable and emit reconciliation metrics and traces
Platform-FE Team | 2026-03-26 | Console UX: surface 'pin symmetry' warnings and show per-replica pin state in rollout UI
SRE | 2026-03-12 | Create runbook for 'stuck pin' scenarios with step-by-step manual recovery commands and low-risk mitigation playbook
notes: 2026-03-05 - Replicated the race in staging with a two-controller parallel update test; confirmed missing transactional guard in pin controller
2026-03-06 - Design review: decided to add a reconciliation loop + leader-elected sweeper to avoid global locks; trade-off: small delay for eventual consistency vs. risk of lock contention
2026-03-09 - PR #882 opened implementing idempotent unpin and traceable reconciliation steps; currently under code review
2026-03-11 - Security review: no secrets exposed; KMS interactions not impacted by this change
2026-03-12 - SRE added alert for 'pin asymmetry' when >1 replica disagrees on per-route pin state
